title: P2.3.1a — Direct-host WebMCP invocation-signal compatibility correction
body:
Parent: #1212. Coordination: #1209. Predecessor: completed #1271 / merged #1272. Evaluation blocker: #1273.

## Purpose

Correct one bounded compatibility defect exposed by the first direct ChatGPT desktop Site-tool evaluation attempt.

The merged P2.3.1 tool `augnes_get_current_work_context` is discovered correctly by ChatGPT desktop Site tools and was selected by the fixed R1 prompt, but direct execution failed before the authenticated GET with:

`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aborted')`

Diagnostics under #1273 reproduced that exact message when the tool callback receives an invocation-options object with `signal` absent/undefined.

This issue is a product compatibility correction only. It is not a model-selection evaluation and must not consume any P2.3.2 fixed case.

## Proven diagnostic facts

- Current canonical main at diagnosis: `9b0d3f2b57fa387e6887b8e3e4f8ecc139bb12e0`
- Tree: `f7710946c61f5bdbe5b01c667ec41951d7cd6460`
- Worktree was clean.
- Direct ChatGPT desktop built-in browser discovered exactly one Site tool:
  - title: `Read current Augnes work`
  - name: `augnes_get_current_work_context`
  - 1 read / 0 write
- R1 selected the Site tool.
- Direct execution failed before the authenticated GET.
- Local unchanged-source reproduction:
  - valid `{ signal }` -> `current_work_context`, one read
  - `{}` -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aborted')`, zero reads
  - `undefined` or omitted second argument -> `TypeError: ... (reading 'signal')`, zero reads
  - `{ signal: undefined }` -> same `reading 'aborted'` failure
  - already-aborted valid signal -> `read_cancelled`, zero reads
- The authenticated route/projector remains healthy with a valid signal:
  - HTTP 200
  - exact current-work/project/packet projection
  - exactly two selected excerpts
  - known timestamp versus null/unknown preserved
  - serialized SQLite bytes unchanged, including session rows
  - zero provider/external calls
- Therefore:
  - `AUGNES_INVOCATION_OPTIONS_ASSUMPTION`: proven
  - `BOUNDARY_COMPATIBILITY_GAP`: supported
  - `DIRECT_HOST_SIGNAL_OMISSION`: strongly suggested, not directly observed

The documented WebMCP callback contract may require a signal. That does not establish what the ChatGPT desktop Site-tools host actually supplied.

## Scope

Make the smallest compatibility correction at the WebMCP invocation boundary.

Do not change:

- tool name
- title
- description
- input schema
- annotations
- route
- projector fields
- currentness semantics
- stale-binding semantics
- selected-source admission
- semantic/execution authority flags
- App/MCP tool lists
- Site configuration
- installed Companion
- P2.3.2 fixed prompts or expected labels

Do not add retries, automatic refresh, writes, source fetches, provider calls or another authority owner.

## Required behavior

Normalize invocation cancellation context once at callback entry.

1. If the host supplies a valid `AbortSignal`, preserve and use that signal.
2. If invocation options are absent, or `signal` is absent/undefined, use a local per-invocation non-aborted fallback signal.
3. If a signal value is present but malformed/non-signal, fail closed with a bounded existing refusal class and perform zero reads. Do not reinterpret malformed host state as user arguments or authority.
4. Use the normalized signal consistently for:
   - pre-read cancellation check
   - authenticated GET
   - post-read cancellation check
   - catch/refusal classification
5. Keep the separate registration-lifetime AbortController and stale-binding checks unchanged.
6. A missing host signal means host cancellation is unavailable for that invocation; do not claim otherwise.

Prefer no new public result field/status unless existing bounded refusal classes are insufficient.

## Required regression coverage

Add explicit unchanged-contract tests for:

- valid `{ signal }`
- `{}`
- `undefined`
- omitted second argument
- `{ signal: undefined }`
- present malformed/non-AbortSignal signal -> bounded refusal, zero reads
- valid signal identity preserved
- already-aborted signal -> `read_cancelled`, zero reads
- in-flight cancellation with valid host signal
- disposal before invocation
- disposal during a fallback-signal read
- binding replacement/stale project or packet with omitted invocation signal
- authentication failure, malformed JSON and unrelated read failures retain bounded refusal behavior
- successful fallback invocation preserves:
  - exact work binding
  - two-source projection
  - known/null observation-time behavior
  - `unresolved_scope: not_projected`
  - untrusted source semantics
  - false semantic/execution authority
  - zero read-attributable DB-byte changes

## Qualification

Re-run the existing deterministic P2.3.1 source/authenticated owner tests and the current native Chrome qualification appropriate to the repository.

Under the revised user-authorized verification protocol, additionally compare the same disposable registered-tool harness and invocation shapes across merged #1272/base, the corrected PR head, and a non-persistent mutant that bypasses only invocation-signal normalization. The key `execute({}, {})` probe must reproduce the exact original exception with zero reads on base, succeed with one authenticated read on head, and reproduce the exception with zero reads on the mutant. Preserve cancellation, stale refusal, result/authority invariants, zero read-attributable DB changes and zero provider/external calls. Remove the mutant and retain the exact clean PR head.

If that causal chain and existing regression/native/exact-head verification pass, direct ChatGPT desktop post-fix re-execution is **confirmatory residual evidence, not the sole proof of correction or sole merge gate**. A merge-readiness recommendation must still state that desktop post-fix execution is unobserved, that actual host callback arguments were not captured, and that separate host integration failures remain possible. This does not authorize merge or Ready status.

A future **separate non-evaluation direct-host compatibility smoke**, when separately resumed and the operator is available, should use a fresh disposable runtime and may explicitly request the known tool. Confirm the same descriptor, execution without the prior exception, expected bounded result and zero read-attributable writes. It must not consume R1–R4/N1–N4/STALE and cannot count as selection evidence. Human app-shell assistance is permitted only through normal UI; do not bypass protected desktop control restrictions.

## Evaluation integrity

The original #1273 campaign is stopped.

Its R1 result remains:

- selection observed
- direct Site-tool execution failed
- fallback answer succeeded through other paths

Do not relabel that R1 as a pass after this correction.

After this issue is corrected and qualified, #1273 must restart as a **fresh campaign** with a fresh disposable evaluation runtime/fixture and all fixed cases allocated anew. Do not silently continue from old R1.

## Expected repository outcome

A narrow source/test correction, verification record if needed by repository convention, focused qualification, then Draft PR for review.

Do not merge or mark Ready automatically.
